title: JUDGE-2x2: is the judge limited by its own ability to solve the question, or only by the reference? (zero calls; the clean 2x2 that retires Probe B's confound)
question: Verdict accuracy on the discriminating questions conditioned on BOTH whether the judge model itself solved the question and whether the reference was right, for the pairwise and the pointwise format.

sentence_of_record: JUDGE-2x2 (2026-09-14, zero calls): holding the reference fixed, judge ability makes no difference: pairwise 0.780 (judge solved) vs 0.796 (judge failed) when the reference is right; pointwise 0.854 vs 0.837; when the reference is wrong 0.250 / 0.145 and 0.417 / 0.130. Probe B's capability effect was entirely the reference confound: a cheap judge does not need to solve the question, it needs the right answer. Validates the cheap-judge architecture.

plain_description.what: No calls. Judge accuracy on discriminating questions was split four ways: whether the judge model could solve the question itself, crossed with whether the reference answer was right. Done for the pairwise and grading formats.
plain_description.why: It asks whether a cheap judge must be smart enough to solve the question, or only needs a correct reference.
plain_description.information: If judge ability mattered at a fixed reference, cheap judges would be risky. If only the reference matters, a cheap judge plus a good reference is enough. Result: done, descriptive. With the reference held fixed, judge ability made no difference (for example 0.78 vs 0.80 accuracy when the reference is right). A wrong reference drives accuracy down sharply. This supports the cheap-judge design. Note: older question pool, ruled 'history, not evidence'.
